questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Fill up (Structure): HBV is a DNA ______ virus; its genome is partially double stranded, ______ circular dsDNA.
questions.exp: 'DNA : Hepadnavirus. Partially double stranded : Relaxed circular dsDNA.' Figure caption: 'Relaxed circular dsDNA'. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Match — 1) Incomplete (+) strand 2) Complete (−) strand … A) Reverse transcriptase / polymerase B) Primer
questions.exp: 'Incomplete (+) strand : primer; Complete (−) strand : Reverse transcriptase / polymerase.' (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Infective virion size and name, number of genotypes, and number of ORFs — as printed?
questions.exp: 'Infective particle (virion) : 42 nm Dane particle; 10 genotypes in HBV; 4 open reading frames (ORFs)'. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Which ORF label does NOT appear in the circular genome figure?
questions.exp: Figure labels: ORF Pre S1, ORF Pre S2, HBsAg gene, ORF S, ORF P, Polymerase gene, ORF X, ORF Core, Pre C. There is no separate 'ORF E'. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Gene table — match — 1) S-gene 2) C-gene 3) Pre C-gene … A) HBeAg, qualitative marker of infectivity & replication B) HBsAg, surface protein C) HBcAg, core protein (intracellular; anti-HBcAg in blood)
questions.exp: S-gene → HBsAg surface protein; C-gene → HBcAg core protein (intracellular; anti-HBcAg in blood); Pre C-gene (part of C-gene) → HBeAg qualitative marker of infectivity & replication. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Gene table continued — match — 1) P-gene 2) X-gene … A) HBx Ag, associated with hepatocellular carcinoma B) Polymerase, reverse transcriptase enzyme
questions.exp: P-gene → polymerase / reverse transcriptase enzyme; X-gene → HBx Ag associated with HCC. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Judge from the table: I HBcAg is intracellular and only its antibody is detected in blood. II HBeAg is a quantitative marker of replication.
questions.exp: 'Core protein (Intracellular anti-HBcAg : in blood)'; HBeAg is the 'Qualitative marker of infectivity & replication' (HBV DNA is the quantitative marker, p1037). (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Progression diagram: incubation period, and the outcome percentages after acute hepatitis?
questions.exp: 'Virus entry —60 days Incubation Period (IP)→ Acute hepatitis → 95–99% Recovery / 1–5% Chronic hepatitis'. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Fill up: In the progression diagram, chronic hepatitis follows ______ transmission in ______%.
questions.exp: '95% Vertical transmission' arrow into Chronic hepatitis. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three end-points drawn from cirrhosis in the progression diagram?
questions.exp: Cirrhosis → Portal hypertension; Hepatocellular carcinoma; Liver failure. Notes: 'Also seen: NASH' (direct HCC arrow) and 'No treatment available.' (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Infectivity of HBV relative to HIV and HCV, as printed?
questions.exp: '100x as HIV, 10x as HCV'. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: Genotype notes — match — 1) HAV 2) HEV 3) HBV commonest genotype 4) HBV HCC-risk genotype … A) 4 genotypes B) Genotype C C) 1 genotype D) Genotype A
questions.exp: '1 genotype in HAV, 4 in HEV → Commonest : Genotype A; HCC risk : Genotype C'. (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: HBV is 'found in all body fluids except ______'.
questions.exp: 'Found in all body fluids except stools.' (Book p1036)

questions.sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10
questions.q: A pregnant woman is HBsAg-positive. Applying the printed 90/10 rule, what determines whether transmission risk is 90% or 10%?
questions.exp: 'Pregnancy : 90/10 rule — HBsAg +ve + HBeAg +ve : 90% chance of transmission; HBeAg −ve : 10% chance.' (Book p1036)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Mode of transmission tree for acute hepatitis B — which is NOT one of the four printed arms?
questions.exp: Arms: Vertical, Percutaneous, Sexual, Blood transfusion. 'No feco-oral / breast milk transmission.' (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Percutaneous risk figures printed for HBV and HCV?
questions.exp: 'Percutaneous — Risk : 6 – 30%; HCV Risk : 0.6 – 6.1%'. (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Judge: I Sexual transmission risk is printed as 'not established'. II Blood-transfusion risk is 1 : 200,000 units and 1 : 1,800,000 with HBV > HBC (HCV).
questions.exp: 'Sexual : Not established'; 'Blood Transfusion : 1 : 200000 units; 1 : 1800000 [HBV > HBC]'. (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Post-transfusion hepatitis — which hierarchy of agents is printed?
questions.exp: 'Post Transfusion Hepatitis : Hepatitis following transfusion • CMV > EBV > HCV.' (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Symptoms of acute hepatitis B: duration of prodrome and when it appears?
opts: No prodrome; abrupt jaundice at 60 days
2–3 days of prodromal phase after 60 days of IP
2–3 weeks of prodrome after 30 days IP
7 days of prodrome after 40 days IP
questions.exp: '2–3 days of prodromal phase after 60 days of IP. Jaundice + ↑↑ enzymes (ALT/AST).' (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Investigations — match — 1) Anti-HAV IgM 2) Anti-HEV IgM … A) m/c cause in adults B) m/c cause in children
questions.exp: 'Anti-HAV IgM (m/c cause : children). Anti-HEV IgM (m/c cause : adults). if both −ve → HBsAg, HBeAg, anti-HBc IgM.' (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: HBV marker curve — match — 1) dark blue 2) red 3) green 4) purple … A) Anti-HBs B) HBsAg C) Total anti-HBc D) IgM anti-HBc
questions.exp: Legend: HBsAg (blue), IgM Anti-HBc (red), Total Anti-HBc (green), Anti-HBs (purple). (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: On the 'HBV infection markers' graph, the boxed window period sits between which weeks after exposure?
questions.exp: The 'Window period' box lies over the 24–32-week span, after HBsAg falls and before anti-HBs rises; upper bands show HBeAg then Anti-HBe. (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Interpretation table — match — 1) HBsAg +, HBeAg +, anti-HBc IgM + 2) HBsAg +, HBeAg −, anti-HBc IgM + … A) Low infectivity & replication / pre-core gene mutant (unable to express HBeAg) B) Acute hepatitis with ↑ infectivity & replication
questions.exp: Column 1 (all +): acute hepatitis with ↑ infectivity & replication. Column 2 (HBeAg −): low infectivity & replication / Pre core gene mutant unable to express HBeAg. (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Fill up (right-hand bullets): S gene / A gene / Escape / Occult gene mutation → ↓ viral load, won't express ______; best test: ______.
questions.exp: 'Sgene/A gene/Escape/Occult gene mutation : ↓ viral load – Won't express HBsAg. Best test : Anti HBc IgM.' (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: Basal core mutant expresses what percentage of HBeAg, per the bullet?
questions.exp: 'Basal core mutant : Express 30% of HBeAg.' (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation
questions.q: What is printed as the best marker for acute hepatitis at the bottom of the page?
questions.exp: 'Best marker for acute hepatitis : HBV DNA load (Quantitative marker).' (Anti-HBc IgM is the best test for escape/occult mutants.) (Book p1037)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Progression table — match — 1) Recovery 2) Chronic hepatitis 3) AFH with simple HBV infection 4) AFH with HBV + HDV co-infection … A) 5–20% B) 0.1–1% C) 95–99% D) 1–5%
questions.exp: Recovery 95–99%; Chronic hepatitis 1–5%; Acute fulminant hepatitis: simple HBV 0.1–1%, HBV + HDV coinfection 5–20%. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Follow-up is done after how long, per the printed bullet?
opts: 24 weeks of symptom onset / 12–16 weeks since IP
24 weeks since IP / 12–16 weeks of symptom onset
6 weeks since IP / 2 weeks of symptoms
questions.exp: 'After 24 weeks since IP/12–16 wks of symptom onset'. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Follow-up conversions — match — 1) HBsAg 2) Anti-HBc IgG 3) HBeAg … A) converts to anti-HBeAg B) converts to anti-HBsAg C) converts to anti-HBc IgM (as printed)
questions.exp: Printed: 'HBsAg converts→ anti HBsAg; Anti HBc IgG converts→ Anti HBc IgM; HBeAg → anti HBeAg' — all three bracketed as Recovery. (Note: the printed IgG→IgM direction is the reverse of the usual IgM→IgG class switch; taught here as written.) (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Per the follow-up bullet, which serological pair defines chronic hepatitis?
questions.exp: 'HBsAg +ve, anti HBc IgG +ve : Chronic hepatitis'. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Chronic hepatitis profile: HBsAg + and anti-HBc IgG +; HBeAg is POSITIVE. What HBV DNA threshold and interpretation does the flowchart give?
opts: HBV DNA load < 2,000 IU/mL — low infectivity, carrier state
HBV DNA at any level — carrier, no need of Rx but HCC risk
HBV DNA load > 20,000 IU/mL — high infectivity, high replication
HBV DNA load > 2,000 IU/mL — high infectivity, high replication
questions.exp: '+ve → HBV DNA load > 20000 IU/mL → High infectivity, high replication'. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: HBeAg NEGATIVE branch — match — 1) HBV DNA > 2,000 IU/mL 2) HBV DNA < 2,000 IU/mL … A) Low infectivity, low replication → carriers B) High infectivity, high replication
questions.exp: HBeAg −ve: HBV DNA > 2000 → high infectivity/replication; < 2000 → low infectivity/replication → Carriers. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Carriers (HBeAg −, DNA < 2000) — judge: I No need of Rx. II No risk for HCC.
questions.exp: 'Carriers → No need of Rx; Risk for HCC.' (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Pre-core / basal core mutant carries a very poor prognosis with ↑ risk for three outcomes. Which is NOT listed?
questions.exp: 'Pre-Core / Basal Core mutant : very poor prognosis; ↑ risk for HCC, Cirrhosis, Decompensation.' (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Serological patterns table — match — 1) HBsAg + / anti-HBs − / anti-HBc IgM / HBeAg + / anti-HBe − 2) HBsAg + / anti-HBs − / anti-HBc IgG / HBeAg + / anti-HBe − … A) Chronic hepatitis B, high infectivity B) Acute hepatitis B, high infectivity
questions.exp: Row 1: acute hepatitis B, high infectivity (IgM). Row 2: chronic hepatitis B, high infectivity (IgG). (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Serology: HBsAg +, anti-HBs −, anti-HBc IgG, HBeAg −, anti-HBe −. Give the two printed interpretations and the confirmatory step.
opts: Window period of seroconversion from HBsAg to anti-HBs, OR heterotypic anti-HBs — repeat anti-HBs in 4 weeks
Recovery from hepatitis B, OR hepatitis B in the remote past — no further test is needed
Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B, OR escape mutant — do anti-HBc IgM to confirm
Late acute or chronic hepatitis B with low infectivity, OR HBeAg-negative (precore-mutant) hepatitis B — do HBV DNA to confirm
questions.exp: Row 3: '1. Late acute or chronic hepatitis B, low infectivity 2. HBeAg negative (Precore-mutant) hepatitis B (Chronic or, rarely, acute). Do HBV DNA to confirm'. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Serology: HBsAg +, anti-HBs +, anti-HBc +, HBeAg ±, anti-HBe ±. Which pair of interpretations is printed, and which is labelled common vs rare?
opts: Immunisation with HBsAg vaccine plus passive HBIG (common); occult HBV with low viral load (rare)
HBsAg of one subtype with heterotypic anti-HBs (common); seroconversion from HBsAg to anti-HBs in progress (rare, window period)
Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B (common); S-gene escape mutant that fails to express HBsAg (rare)
Recovery from hepatitis B with persisting antigenaemia (common); hepatitis B in the remote past (rare)
questions.exp: Row 4: '1. HBsAg of one subtype and heterotypic anti-HBs (common) 2. Process of seroconversion from HBsAg to anti HBs (rare) (window period)'. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Serology: HBsAg −, anti-HBs −, anti-HBc IgM, HBeAg ±, anti-HBe ±. Interpretation?
opts: Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B
questions.exp: Row 5: 'Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B'. (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Last three rows — match — 1) HBsAg −, anti-HBs −, anti-HBc IgG, HBeAg −, anti-HBe ± 2) HBsAg −, anti-HBs +, anti-HBc IgG, HBeAg −, anti-HBe ± 3) HBsAg −, anti-HBs +, anti-HBc −, HBeAg −, anti-HBe − … A) Recovery from hepatitis B B) Immunisation with HBsAg (after vaccination) C) Hepatitis B in remote past, or escape mutant
questions.exp: Row 6: remote past / escape mutant (anti-HBc alone). Row 7: recovery (anti-HBs + anti-HBc). Row 8: immunisation (anti-HBs alone). (Book p1038)

questions.sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table
questions.q: Which single-marker pattern distinguishes vaccination from natural recovery in the serological table?
opts: Anti-HBe is present after vaccination but absent after recovery
Anti-HBc is absent after vaccination but present after recovery
questions.exp: Immunisation row: anti-HBs + with anti-HBc −; recovery row: anti-HBs + with anti-HBc IgG. (Book p1038)

units.title: HBV structure, genes and natural history
units.guide: Hepadnavirus, relaxed circular partially dsDNA, (+) incomplete primer / (−) complete RT; 42 nm Dane, 10 genotypes, 4 ORFs; S→HBsAg, C→HBcAg (intracellular), pre-C→HBeAg qualitative, P→polymerase/RT, X→HBxAg HCC; 60-day IP, 95–99% recovery, 1–5% chronic (95% vertical), cirrhosis → PHTN/HCC/liver failure, NASH also, no treatment; 100× HIV, 10× HCV; HAV 1, HEV 4 genotypes, A commonest, C HCC; all fluids except stool; 90/10 rule by HBeAg.

units.title: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, symptoms, markers and interpretation
units.guide: Vertical, percutaneous 6–30% (HCV 0.6–6.1%), sexual not established, transfusion 1:200,000 & 1:1,800,000 HBV>HCV; no feco-oral/breast milk; post-transfusion CMV>EBV>HCV; 2–3 day prodrome after 60 days; anti-HAV IgM children, anti-HEV IgM adults → HBsAg/HBeAg/anti-HBc IgM; marker curve colours and 24–32 wk window; HBeAg + vs − interpretation, pre-core mutant; S/escape/occult mutants lose HBsAg, best test anti-HBc IgM; basal core mutant 30% HBeAg; HBV DNA best acute marker.

units.title: Progression, follow-up, chronic profile and serological patterns
units.guide: Recovery 95–99%, chronic 1–5%, AFH 0.1–1% vs 5–20% with HDV; follow-up 24 wk/12–16 wk; conversions to anti-HBs, anti-HBc IgM (as printed), anti-HBe = recovery; HBsAg + anti-HBc IgG = chronic; HBeAg + → DNA >20,000; HBeAg − → >2,000 high vs <2,000 carriers (no Rx, HCC risk); pre-core/basal core mutant poor prognosis; 8-row serological pattern table including window, reactivation, remote/escape, recovery, immunisation.
